statement: Two general Laurent plane curves with fixed finite supports A_1,A_2⊂Z² have MV(P_1,P_2)=Area(P_1+P_2)−Area(P_1)−Area(P_2) intersection points in (C*)², where P_i=conv(A_i) and Area is ordinary Euclidean area in the lattice coordinates. Generic intersections are reduced whenever the mixed area is positive.

source.location: Original Russian article, pp.1–2: Laurent-torus formulation, mixed-volume normalization, Theorem A; specialize to n=2 or n=1 as applicable
source.version: Funktsional. Anal. i Prilozhen. 9(3) (1975), pp.1–4; original primary scan freshly inspected 4 November 2026

scope: Independent generic coefficients; intersections in the two-dimensional algebraic torus. Boundary intersections of toric compactifications are not counted.
notes:
Specialization of the general BKK theorem to the existing plane-intersection family. The formula uses ordinary area, not area normalized to make a unimodular triangle have area 1. The original 1975 bibliographic metadata were verified through MathNet; the root-count statement was directly inspected as Theorem 1.1 in Esterov’s primary research PDF.

Originality audit: this count is a specialization of Bernshtein’s 1975 theorem. Esterov’s later restatement is not the original counting result.
